summary: Blink timer of a small embedded text element: counts down and every 30 frames flips between two 0x24-byte layout-animation parameter blocks, giving a flashing label/cursor.
evidence: Ui_TextBlink_Update (0x00229BF4) is called on embedded elements inside pages (Ui_MenuUpdate passes &self->f_e20, Ui_JumonWindow_DispatchModeHandler &self->f_b5c), and the sibling 0x0022A8A4 uses the same fields to show a fixed sprite and mark the element idle (f_98 = -1). The struct is therefore a small embedded timer, not a standalone Ui_Object.

fields.name: layerIndex
fields.evidence: Update passes (u32)self->f_28 << 0x10 as the element key to 0x001A6680 and the sibling page code builds 'self->f_28 << 16 | paneIndex'; the same packing is documented for Ui_TextElement_SetString (0x003A7A2C) and Ui_Pane_PlayLayoutAnim, so this u16 is the high (layer) half of the packed text/pane id.

fields.name: blockIndex
fields.evidence: 'iVar1 = 1 - *(int *)(param_1 + 0x94); *(int *)(param_1 + 0x94) = iVar1;' then the block 'self + iVar1 * 0x24 + 0x50' is passed to 0x001A6680 - index of the active one of the two 0x24-byte animation parameter blocks.

fields.name: blinkTimer
fields.evidence: Counted down each frame ('self->f_98 = self->f_98 + -1'); when it reaches 0 the block flips and it is reloaded with 0x1e (30 frames). The sibling indicator disables the effect with 'self->f_98 = 0xffffffff'.

summary: Text box pane state with three colour slots 0x20 bytes apart, one per text line; the reset helper writes the same colour into all three and returns it converted.
evidence: Ui_TextBox_ResetLineColors (0x0053ADA0) stores r3 into self+0x634, +0x654 and +0x674 and optionally converts r1 through 0x0055861C; the class is the 1656-byte (0x678) BFLYT 'txt1' text box whose ctor is Ui_LayoutTextBox_Ctor (0x0053E4D4, vtable 0x00781498).

fields.name: lineColor0
fields.evidence: '*(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x634) = param_4;' in Ui_TextBox_ResetLineColors; first of three slots spaced 0x20 bytes apart, so each line entry is larger than the colour word the batch recorded.

fields.name: lineColor1
fields.evidence: '*(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x654) = param_4;' in Ui_TextBox_ResetLineColors; second line slot, 0x20 bytes after +0x634.

fields.name: lineColor2
fields.evidence: '*(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x674) = param_4;' in Ui_TextBox_ResetLineColors; third line slot, 0x20 bytes after +0x654 and 4 bytes before the recorded 0x678 size.

summary: Message-label formatter state: a sprite-span id plus two flags that decide whether the message text and an exclamation/question mark are pushed into the global message format slots.
evidence: Ui_TextFormat_FormatWideString (0x0028B858) reads self+0x208 as a Ui_SpriteSpan_Select id, gates the text argument on +0x20A and picks between the wide literals at 0x007BE77C (U+FF1F '？') and 0x007BE780 (U+FF01 '！') with +0x20B, then calls Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset (0x006D3EA0) for slots 5 and 2.

fields.name: spriteId
fields.evidence: 'Ui_SpriteSpan_Select(auStack_48,self->f_208);' - Ui_SpriteSpan_Select (0x0028DDB0, doc: resolves a sprite/format id into three sub-image pointers) takes this u16 as its numberId.

fields.name: maybe_isTextSkipped
fields.evidence: 'if (*(char *)(param_1 + 0x20a) == '\0') { ... Ui_SpriteSpan_Select ...; Message_FormatArgSlot_Reset(2,...); }' - when nonzero the message line is not resolved and format slot 2 is left alone.

fields.name: isQuestionMark
fields.evidence: The u8 chooses the wide punctuation literal used as the '%ls' argument of slot 5: nonzero takes 0x007BE77C (0xFF1F '？'), zero takes 0x007BE780 (0xFF01 '！').

summary: Training-window part: a Ui_Object laid out like Ui_WindowPart that installs its own vtable and the embedded anim-ref/timer widget at +0x11C with a 22-entry 0x18-byte callback table.
evidence: Ui_TrainingWindowPart_Ctor (0x0026423C) duplicates Ui_WindowPart_Ctor (0x0025EB88) with vtable 0x0075CC00 and 0x16 (22) entries instead of 0x3E (62); it calls Ui_Object_CtorBase through 0x001D8B6C and Ui_Object_InitMemberPair(self+0x11C), and is used by maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Ctor.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: *puVar2 = 0x0075CC00 in Ui_TrainingWindowPart_Ctor; the table's slots are Ui_TrainingWindow_InitPanes (0x00261BAC), maybe_Ui_FrameScript_Update (0x00261F40) and Ui_TrainingWindow_UpdateInput (0x00261DC4).

fields.name: unknown_20
fields.evidence: Only evidence is 'puVar3[8] = puVar2', but puVar3 is the member object returned for self+0x11C, so that write lands at self+0x13C. The real base-class word at self+0x20 is never touched by this batch (same finding as S_126 for Ui_WindowPart).

fields.name: widget
fields.evidence: Ui_Object_InitMemberPair(self+0x11C) initialises an embedded member: its vtable 0x0075A93C is stored there, the owner back-pointer at member+0x20 (self+0x13C) and a 22-entry 0x18-byte table at member+0x24 (self+0x140).

summary: Two-line numbered text window: binds txt_l1/txt_l2 and their null_txt overlays and seeds a full-width '01' digit buffer; the three recorded offsets are vtable slots, not data members.
evidence: Ui_TwoLineTextWindow2_Init (0x004D3CC8) calls drN then dispatches (**(code **)(*self + 0x34))/+0x38/+0x48 with the strings txt_l1 (0x004D3DAC), txt_l2 (0x004D3DC0), null_txt_l1 (0x004D3DC8), null_txt_l2 (0x004D3DD4) and the '01' seed 0x304F3055.

fields.name: unknown_d0
fields.evidence: The only evidence '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x34))' is the vtable slot at +0x34 invoked with the txt_l1 string, not a read of self+0xD0; no real field at +0xD0 was recovered.

fields.name: unknown_e0
fields.evidence: The only evidence '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x38))' is the vtable slot at +0x38 bound to the null_txt overlays, not a read of self+0xE0.

fields.name: unknown_120
fields.evidence: The only evidence '(**(code **)(*param_1 + 0x48))(param_1, (u16)self+0x28 << 16)' is the vtable slot at +0x48 receiving the packed (layer<<16) key, not a read of self+0x120.

summary: UI object that owns five 0x50-byte Ui_AnimRefList entries at +0x4C; used as the animatable base of text widgets.
evidence: Ui_Widget5Anim_Ctor (0x002B761C) runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, stores vtable 0x0075F7F8 and calls std_ConstructArray(self+0x4C, Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor 0x003E0454, 0x50, 5); its only caller is maybe_Ui_TextWidget_Ctor. Ui_AnimRefList is 80 bytes (0x50) in structs.json, matching the element size.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: *puVar1 = 0x0075F7F8 after Ui_Object_CtorBase; the table at 0x0075F7F8 has slots Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, maybe_Ui_SetThreeObjectVisibility, Ui_Pane_SetVisibleWithAnim, Ui_SelectList_InitPanes.

fields.name: unknown_08
fields.evidence: The evidence 'FUN_0062ab3c(puVar4[2],uVar5)' belongs to maybe_Ui_Widget5Anim_CreateItems, where puVar4 is a freshly allocated 0x1C-byte item with vtable 0x00782950, not this object; no access to self+0x08 was recovered.

fields.name: animRefLists
fields.evidence: std_ConstructArray(puVar1 + 0x13 (= +0x4C), 0x003E0454 Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor, 0x50, 5) default-constructs five 0x50-byte anim-ref lists starting here.

summary: Ten-row list widget: a Ui_Object with an embedded row table at +0x54 (vtable 0x0077F71C, count 10) and ten 0x18-byte row records at +0x70.
evidence: maybe_Ui_WidgetWith10Rows_Ctor (0x002AC7EC) runs Ui_Object_CtorSmallB (Ui_Object_CtorBase), writes vtable 0x00760350, initialises the embedded table at +0x54 through 0x00622248, stores 10 at +0x6C, the table vtable 0x0077F71C at +0x54 and constructs ten 0x18-byte records at +0x70.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: '*puVar2 = uRam002ac840' where uRam002ac840 = 0x00760350, written right after Ui_Object_CtorSmallB; the same literal is used by Ui_WidgetWith12Rows.

fields.name: unknown_18
fields.evidence: 'puVar2[6] = 10' is written 0x18 bytes into the sub-object that starts at self+0x54, i.e. at self+0x6C (real row count), not at self+0x18.

fields.name: maybe_rowTable
fields.evidence: 'puVar2 = FUN_00622248(puVar2 + 0x15)' initialises the embedded table at +0x54; the ctor then stores its vtable 0x0077F71C there and builds ten 0x18-byte rows at +0x70. The initialiser 0x00622248 is unnamed, so the exact type is unknown.

summary: Twelve-row list widget: a Ui_Object with an embedded row table at +0x54 (vtable 0x0077F71C, count 12) and twelve 0x18-byte row records at +0x70.
evidence: maybe_Ui_WidgetWith12Rows_Ctor (0x0029DD44) is the same body as Ui_WidgetWith10Rows_Ctor with 0xc (12) instead of 10: Ui_Object_CtorBase, vtable 0x00760350, table at +0x54 via 0x00622248, table vtable 0x0077F71C, twelve 0x18-byte rows at +0x70.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: '*puVar2 = uRam0029dd98' writes the class vtable right after Ui_Object_CtorBase; it is the 12-row sibling of the 10-row widget's table.

fields.name: unknown_18
fields.evidence: 'puVar2[6] = 0xc' is written 0x18 bytes into the sub-object starting at self+0x54 (i.e. self+0x6C), where the row count lives, not at self+0x18.

fields.name: maybe_rowTable
fields.evidence: 'puVar2 = FUN_00622248(puVar2 + 0x15)' initialises the embedded row table at +0x54, which gets vtable 0x0077F71C and twelve 0x18-byte rows at +0x70; the initialiser is unnamed.

summary: Tiny holder that lazily activates one child window (a 0x3E0-byte dive-start window variant) through Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable and deletes it on teardown.
evidence: Ui_WindowHolder_Ctor (0x002C1C08) stores vtable 0x00760004, clears the byte at +4 and the pointer at +8, allocates 0x3E0 bytes (Mem_AllocAligned_2), constructs Ui_DiveStartWindow_VariantCtor, registers it with Ui_Object_CreatePartsFromTable and activates it (+0x94 = 1). CheckReady (0x002C1BC0) and DtorDelete (0x002C1CB8) only touch +4, +8 and the child.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: '*param_1 = DAT_002c1cf4' (0x00760004) in both Ui_WindowHolder_Ctor and Ui_WindowHolder_DtorDelete; the vtable's slots include maybe_Ui_WindowHolder_CheckReady.

fields.name: childWindow
fields.evidence: Ctor stores the created 0x3E0-byte Ui_DiveStartWindow variant here ('self[2] = uVar3'), DtorDelete releases it through Ui_List_ReleaseEntries and clears it, and CheckReady reads its +0x94 active byte.

fields.name: unknown_30
fields.evidence: The only evidence 'uVar3 = (**(code **)(*param_1 + 0xc))(param_1)' is a call through vtable slot +0xC, not a field read at self+0x30.

summary: Action-pane animator family: a Battle_ActionAnimEntry-derived animator carrying the action id/name and per-track animation parameters; several batch methods are actually action-window helpers, so the class is loose.
evidence: Ui_ActionPane_Init (0x00193CE4) installs the pane vtable pair 0x00758AE0/0x00782740, copies the 15-byte name and stores the action id; the derived ctors 0x003646B4 (vtable 0x00765240, id at +0x28, 0.26f at +0x2C) and 0x003A4EC8 (vtable 0x0076819C, track parameters +0x2C..+0x4E) build on it. Ui_ActionPane_InitAnimators/AddReactAnimator are window routines that reference the pane through a pointer.

fields.name: maybe_animFloat
fields.evidence: The derived animator ctor 0x003A4EC8 stores the float constant 0x3FE66666 (1.8f) at +0x48; the batch evidence from Ui_ActionPane_InitAnimators ('Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x4c,self->f_48,4)') comes from a different window object, so the meaning of this float is not pinned down.

fields.name: maybe_actionAnimEntry
fields.evidence: Ui_ActionPane_AddReactAnimator reads 'iVar3 = self->f_60' and then tests iVar3->f_40 (animator count) and replaces animator slot 5, so this word is a pointer to the pane's Battle_ActionAnimEntry list; no writer of self+0x60 was recovered.

summary: Actually a field-actor curve-move action, not a 2D UI actor: it evaluates the embedded curve at +0x58 and applies the resulting point to the target object at +0x28; the generated Ui_Actor2D name is wrong.
evidence: The only method, 0x004134CC, is Field_ActorAction_ApplyCurvePositionC (R3_053): 'Math_Curve_EvaluatePoint(auStack_10,&self->f_58); func_005F3ADC(self->f_28,auStack_10);' and its vtable 0x0076DEE0 sits in a Field_ActorAction table next to Field_ActorAction_SnapshotActorPose. Nothing in the body touches a 2D UI actor.

fields.name: maybe_targetObject
fields.evidence: 'FUN_005f3adc(*(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x28),auStack_10);' passes this pointer together with the evaluated curve point to 0x005F3ADC, so it is the object that receives the position; the callee 0x005F3ADC is unnamed.

fields.name: curve
fields.evidence: 'Math_Curve_EvaluatePoint(auStack_10,&self->f_58)' - Math_Curve_EvaluatePoint (0x006281E4) takes a curve struct whose a..e coefficients live at +0x0..+0x14, max at +0x1C and t at +0x20; +0x58 is the start of that 0x24-byte embedded curve.

summary: UI widget with twelve 0x50-byte Ui_AnimRefList entries at +0x4C; used by shop, item-menu and party-select window parts.
evidence: Ui_LayoutRef12Widget_Ctor (0x002947E8) runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, stores vtable 0x0075DC34, calls std_ConstructArray(self+0x4C, Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor 0x003E0454, 0x50, 12) and zeroes self+0x40C; callers are Ui_ShopWindow_CreateSubObjects, Ui_ItemMenu_RootPart_Ctor and Ui_PartySelectRowWidget_Ctor.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: '*puVar1 = DAT_00294818' (0x0075DC34) after Ui_Object_CtorBase; the table's slots are maybe_Ui_Widget_DtorB/DtorA, Ui_Widget_ReleaseSub, maybe_Ui_Window_SetPaneVisibleThunk and Ui_PartySelectWindow_InitPanes.

fields.name: animRefLists
fields.evidence: std_ConstructArray(self+0x4C, 0x003E0454 Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor, 0x50, 12) constructs twelve 0x50-byte anim-ref lists starting here (end at self+0x40C, which the ctor then zeroes).

summary: Head of an animated UI element: shared UI-object vtable at +0 followed by two linked Ui_AnimRefList members at +8 and +0x64; the generated Ui_AnimRefList 'base' is really the first member constructor.
evidence: Ui_AnimatableElement_Ctor (0x003A5718) writes vtable 0x00759378 (the shared UI object table used by the record-window sub-objects), zeroes self[1], then calls Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor(self+2 = +8) and a second list at +0x64, linking f_60/f_64; since the first list constructor runs on self+8, Ui_AnimRefList is a member type, not a base.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: '*self = 0x00759378' in Ui_AnimatableElement_Ctor; the same literal is used by the record-window sub-objects, and one caller (Ui_TimerDisplay_Ctor 0x00411820) builds the element in place.

fields.name: unknown_04
fields.evidence: The ctor only zeroes it ('self[1] = 0') and nothing in the batch reads it; the follow-up lists start at +8, so its meaning is unrecovered.

summary: Ten-slot display-cell template table (0xB8 bytes per slot) embedded in the status window; each slot begins with 0x0FFFFFFF and is copied from a default template.
evidence: maybe_Ui_CellGrid_InitSlots (0x001932D0) loops from self+0x8BC4 to self+0x92F4 (10 iterations: 0x730 / 0xB8) writing 0x0FFFFFFF and memcpy'ing a 0x84-byte template into each 0xB8-byte slot; its only caller is Ui_StatusWindow_RebuildSceneObjects (0x00343174).

fields.name: cellSlots
fields.evidence: 'puVar1 = (u32 *)(self + 0x8bc4)' starts the slot loop: each iteration writes 0xfffffff, std_memcpy 0x84 bytes of template and fills up to +0xB4, then advances by 0x2E words (0xB8).

fields.name: unknown_end
fields.evidence: The only evidence 'while (puVar2 != (u32 *)(param_1 + 0x92f4))' is the exclusive end address of the 10-slot array (+0x8BC4 + 10*0xB8), not a field; nothing reads a u32 at +0x92F4.

summary: ARM C++ member-function-pointer delegate: a function pointer plus a this-adjustment word (bit 0 marks a virtual call), with bind and invoke helpers.
evidence: Ui_Delegate_BindActionA/B (0x003805B4/0x003805E4) store the 64-bit member-function-pointer pair from the templates at 0x0072ABF8 into +0x10/+0x14; Ui_Delegate_Invoke (0x0038060C) resolves virtual calls via *(code**)(ptr + *(int*)(self + (adj>>1))) exactly as the ARM C++ ABI requires.

fields.name: functionPtr
fields.evidence: Bind methods store the pointer half of the member function pointer here ('*(undefined4 *)(param_1 + 0x10) = *(undefined4 *)(DAT_003805e0 + 8);'); Invoke loads it as a code pointer and calls it.

fields.name: thisAdjust
fields.evidence: Second half of the member function pointer: Invoke tests bit 0 ('tst r0,#1') and, when set, reads the vtable offset from 'self + (f_14 >> 1)' - the standard ARM this-adjustment/virtual flag word.
